analysis:
All reviewed changes are documentation. No code, protocol, key-handling, or authorization behavior changes.

glm53-flash-native.md (new design doc) states the work is in progress, not release-qualified, and that glm5_next stays excluded from EngineV2SupportedModels. It authorizes no rollout. It pins the Hugging Face artifacts by commit revision and says identity, license, tensor coverage and numerical equivalence are separate gates. It says header evidence is not payload hashing. Its state invariants (lines 74-87) require cache identity to bind artifact, quantization, tokenizer/template, layout and the authenticated cache scope. They also require the existing encrypted cache protections (T-041, TB-007) to be preserved and telemetry to carry no prompts, token IDs, media or tool arguments. These are design intents, not implemented controls. The doc keeps the platform repo as owner of catalog and capability work.

build.md (head lines 48-73) says a GLM5Next build does not register the architecture. It says to use the locked Swift-Jinja pin with no dependency patch and not to rewrite another artifact's template. It also adds an SSD test working-volume note and a MiMo scratch-directory/test-binary-identity note.

mimo-prompt-fixtures.md adds tool-schema regression guidance. Its fixture is checksum-pinned and needs no weights or credentials.

Coverage limit: only the metadata unit (67373c0eff1153bd:0) for docs/developer/test.md was supplied. Its large patch is excerpted and truncated, so its content is not reviewed. The docs-only nature makes a security impact unlikely.

Residual gaps (pre-existing, not new):
- Weight-hash enforcement is fail-open (SEC-007, T-027, T-012). A community GLM artifact depends on it.
- When GLM complete-state prefix codecs are implemented, T-041 and TB-007 will need updating. That includes new sparse, recurrent and MTP checkpoint codecs on the encrypted SSD tier.
- The template-parse workaround adds a Hub-supplied chat template to the prompt-contract trust surface.

No findings.
